skill.name: webapp-testing

security_audit.summary: Review found mostly false positives from Markdown backticks and localhost example URLs. The helper script still performs real command execution, including shell-based server startup. Fixed output paths and source-review suppression instructions create additional risk.

remediation.issue: scripts/with_server.py runs server commands with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with argument lists, or validate allowed commands and require confirmation for shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The helper runs arbitrary post-server commands.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict command execution to expected test runners, or document that users must review every command first.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md discourages source review before running scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Remove that instruction and require reviewing bundled scripts and command arguments before execution.

remediation.issue: Examples write screenshots to fixed temp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use project-specific output directories with unique filenames and avoid shared temporary locations for sensitive captures.

remediation.issue: Examples persist console logs and screenshots.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that logs and screenshots may contain secrets, tokens, or private application data.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web apps can be hard to inspect after JavaScript renders the page. This skill guides Playwright automation for screenshots, selector discovery, console logs, and repeatable UI checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides native Python Playwright scripts for local web application testing.
Starts one or more local servers before running a browser automation command.
Captures browser screenshots for visual inspection of rendered pages.
Collects browser console messages during automated page interaction.
Discovers buttons, links, inputs, and selector candidates on a page.
Supports static HTML testing through local file URLs.
limitations: Requires Python Playwright and browser dependencies in the working environment.
Focuses on local development servers and static HTML files.
Helper scripts execute provided commands, so inputs must be trusted.
Example paths and ports usually need project-specific changes.

use_cases.title: Validate Local UI Changes
use_cases.description: Verify interactive UI states on a local development server before committing changes.

use_cases.title: Collect Bug Evidence
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots, console messages, and selector details for reproducible browser bug reports.

use_cases.title: Inspect Static Prototypes
use_cases.description: Open local HTML prototypes, identify controls, and test simple form interactions.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to open my local app, wait for rendering, list visible buttons, links, and inputs, and report useful selectors.

prompt_templates.title: Capture UI Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to capture a full-page screenshot and browser console messages for my local page, then summarize visible errors and warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Run with Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the helper workflow to start my frontend server, wait for the port, run a Playwright check, and stop the server afterward.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Dynamic Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use webapp-testing to inspect a dynamic flow, discover reliable selectors, perform the requested actions, and explain failed waits or missing elements.

output_examples.input: Inspect the local dashboard and identify controls needed for a smoke test.
output: A summary of visible navigation, forms, and buttons.
Recommended selectors for important user actions.
A screenshot location and console warning summary.

output_examples.input: Run a checkout flow check on my development server.
output: Server readiness status and browser actions completed.
Failed wait details if the expected screen does not appear.
Cleanup status after the server stops.

best_practices: Run helpers only in trusted repositories and review commands before execution.
Wait for network idle or a stable selector before inspecting dynamic pages.
Store screenshots and logs in project-specific output folders.
anti_patterns: Running server commands from untrusted prompts or unknown repositories.
Using fixed temporary paths for sensitive screenshots.
Inspecting a rendered page before JavaScript finishes loading.

faq.question: Does this skill test deployed websites?
faq.answer: It is designed for local applications and static HTML. Remote testing needs explicit approval and environment setup.

faq.question: Does it require Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and guidance use Python Playwright with a Chromium browser.

faq.question: Can it start my development server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper can start one or more servers and run a command after ports are ready.

faq.question: Can it capture console logs?
faq.answer: Yes. The console logging example collects browser messages during page interaction.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. The helper can execute server commands, so review commands and source files first.

faq.question: Does it write files?
faq.answer: Yes. Examples save screenshots and logs, so choose safe output paths for sensitive pages.
